item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a node-prefixed rename of every colliding element id in the named fragments; commit 61803a858 applies exactly that and my independent parse finds all 83 new ids prefixed with the file stem and no duplicate new ids.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the rename commit and landing commit, the gate command, and the base/head arms 28 findings EXIT=1 / 0 findings EXIT=0, plus the two scaffolding retries with attributions.

justifications.durability: the repair is a data change with no test file in scope, so it adds no regression test of its own; the guard that keeps future fragments clean is the id-prefix convention in the landing contract plus the scoped audit_fragment_ids this section's sibling node added, which the run's gate exercises — the rename itself is not self-guarding beyond that existing audit.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's gate logs are reproducible: I re-ran the run's own gate.py and read gate-base.log 28 findings EXIT=1 at 07ad28145 and gate-head.log 0 findings EXIT=0 at aa3367847; verify.log records 0 remaining renamed bare ids and 0 remaining href links, and the composed records are clean for eight of the nine plans with the ninth's two residuals (triage-method, triage-keep-budget) documented as an out-of-scope follow-on.
justifications.fit: the prefix is the fragment file's stem, which is the node id the composition keys on, so sibling fragments composed into one record carry distinct anchors; the landing fragment deliberately carries no element ids and therefore adds none to the composition it is checked by, and same-file href anchors were renamed with their targets (the diff contains no href lines because the in-scope fragments held none to rename).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node goal is to rename every colliding element id in the committed fragments so it begins with its fragment's node id, renaming same-file href anchors with it; the diff renames 83 ids across 36 fragments and my probe confirms all 83 new ids begin with the file's stem plus '-', the renamed set is 19 distinct bare ids, and every renamed old id was a genuine duplicate-element-id collision in its plan directory at base while every base collision was renamed (0 mismatches both directions).
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 61803a858 changes exactly the 36 fragments named in the write scope and commit aa3367847 adds only docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/fragment-ids-renamed-batch-c.html; masking every id="..." value makes base and head byte-identical across all 36 files (0 differing), so no prose, attribute or non-colliding id changed, and no plan file was touched.
